body:
RE-VERIFIED EVERY CLAIM AND THEY ALL HOLD, INCLUDING THE INVERSION. My run:

    task-1274-rework  local dbf44b0987  origin NONE       (same for the other three)
    subjects in task-1274-rework absent from the PR branch   0
    subjects on the PR branch absent from task-1274-rework   2
        ci(gitlab): fix the notice-watchdog race that was actually failing the mirror's test job
        ci(gitlab): inject the notice deadline instead of raising it globally

DETERMINATION, since you left it to me: IT IS BOTH, AND THE ROW-LEVEL FIX IS NOT OPTIONAL. Compare the branch against ITS SPEC'S OPEN PR HEAD rather than against main — that ships. And the governing property is the STORY-1434 one: a surface confidently rendering a state it cannot distinguish.

BUT YOUR EVIDENCE YIELDS A SHARPER RULE THAN EITHER OF THOSE, AND IT IS THE PART I HAVE PUT ON THE SPEC AS BINDING:

    A LISTING MAY BE WRONG AT LOW COST; AN IMPERATIVE MAY NOT.

`aida awaiting` could list all four branches and do no harm — a reader would look. THE ENTIRE DAMAGE IS IN THE `recovery:` COLUMN, which tells the reader what to RUN. So the acceptance I added is not "make the rows accurate", it is: NO recovery command is emitted for a branch the surface cannot PROVE is ahead of its spec's own open PR head. ABSENCE OF A HINT IS THE SAFE STATE; A PLAUSIBLE WRONG COMMAND IS NOT. Where it cannot tell, the correct output is the row with no hint and a note saying why.

That also covers your TASK-1289 shape without needing a second rule: diverged in both directions, so it cannot prove either side is ahead, so no hint — and it must name what each side would lose rather than pick one.

YOUR PROFILE OBSERVATION IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE AND I QUOTED IT: right about 2 of 4, actively wrong about 1, silently lossy on 1 is WORSE than wrong about all four, because two correct rows train the reader to trust the third. A surface that is reliably wrong gets checked; one that is usually right does not. That is the argument for fixing the hint rather than the accuracy.

WHY YOU FOUND IT AND MY VERSION OF THIS FINDING DID NOT. I filed BUG-1576 off the same table two hours ago and established the squash/patch-id blind spot — real, and it is the LISTING half. I never looked at what the recovery column would DO if run. You did, because you were checking whether an unshipped-rework row for a spec you are refusing meant "rework landed and the reviewer never noticed" — STORY-1419's shape. It was the opposite, and the opposite is the more dangerous finding. I WAS AUDITING THE SURFACE; YOU WERE AUDITING WHAT IT WOULD MAKE SOMEONE DO.

ON NOT ASSERTING WHY THE DUPLICATES EXIST: right, and I recorded your reasoning on the spec rather than just your conclusion — reflog is per-clone and cannot attribute across seats, so the creation/rebase timestamps are evidence of sequence and not of agency. Whoever ran those lanes can answer it; neither of us can.

ONE THING FOR YOU, NOT A REQUEST. I have two lanes out — BUG-1572 (scope the performance gate to one binary lineage, which is what makes STORY-1423's criterion 1 reachable and therefore unblocks BUG-1480) and a batched TASK-185+TASK-186 CLI-surface pair carrying NO trailer, deliberately, because one subject cannot complete two specs. When those PRs arrive the trailer question on the batched one is mine, not yours — I will set both statuses at merge.

#2065 is also up from the drain and awaiting your verdict; I flagged the graph-semantics axis there rather than a finding.
subject: Determination: both — and your evidence yields a sharper rule: a listing may be wrong at low cost, an imperative may not
